title: PICS-assisted survey reported seven new Large Magellanic Cloud pulsars
summary: A MeerKAT survey of its first four Large Magellanic Cloud pointings reported seven new radio pulsars. The search pipeline applied the Pulsar Image-based Classification System (PICS), a deep-neural image classifier, to folded candidates and retained candidates above a PICS score threshold before human visual classification. The AI narrowed the candidate set (PICS score above 0.1, folded S/N above 7, DM above 3); the survey team then classified the remaining candidates manually and refolded neighbouring beams, and follow-up observations supplied additional checks. Six pulsars were detected again in follow-up; the incoherent-beam pulsar was not. A later paper reports 12 discoveries from additional pointings and timing follow-up of some Paper I pulsars, which are not additional discoveries in this entry.
ai_technology: Pulsar Image-based Classification System (PICS), a deep-neural image classifier for folded candidate plots

source_review.scope: Primary OUP full-text indexed article for candidate selection workflow, score threshold, seven-pulsar result, follow-up status, publication date and first-author affiliation; primary arXiv v1 (2408.04899) and OUP Paper II for version and overlap context. 2026-11-25 correction: arXiv evidence link pointed to the SMC paper (2405.12029); final classification was manual review by the survey team (CandyJar), not volunteers.

evidence.tested: The survey reports seven new LMC radio pulsars. Folded candidates were screened using PICS scores and then visually classified; six of the seven were detected again in follow-up, while the incoherent-beam pulsar was not confirmed in follow-up.
evidence.unknown: PICS filtered candidates but humans classified the candidates as new pulsars. The one incoherent-beam pulsar lacked a follow-up detection in this paper. Later timing work on Paper I objects is not a separate discovery result.
evidence.ai_role: PICS applied a pulsar-like score to folded candidate plots and filtered the survey candidate set before human visual classification; the paper does not attribute final discovery confirmation to the model alone.
